answer: In an agent economy coordinating care for a walnut garden beside a jetty, each agent must lock $100 of collateral for 30 days to receive one daily job slot. Creating more identities grants more slots only if each identity posts its own deposit; splitting one deposit earns nothing extra. An attacker seeking 1,000 slots must therefore immobilize $100,000 for a month, sacrificing liquidity and the returns that capital could earn elsewhere.
